Developers.metaDescription: Submit content for verification and read Zuula fact-checks from your own newsroom tools.

banner.title: Zuula API
banner.description: Submit content for verification and read fact-checks from your own newsroom tools.

preview.title: Preview, subject to change until v1
preview.body: This is an early look at the API for journalists and partners. It is not callable yet: the backend ships in Phase 2, and endpoints, fields and limits may change before version 1.

overview.title: Overview
overview.body: The Zuula API gives accredited journalists and partner organisations the same verification that powers zuula.ug. Checks run asynchronously:
overview.step1: Send content to POST /v1/checks. You get a tracking ID straight away.
overview.step2: Poll GET /v1/checks/[trackingId] until the status is completed.
overview.step3: Read the verdict, confidence score, explanation and citations from the result.
overview.format: JSON over HTTPS (UTF-8). Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.body: Every request needs an API key in the Authorization header. Verified journalists and administrators can create and revoke keys in Account → API access. Keys start with zl_live_ and are shown only once.

scopes.submit: Send text, links, articles and media for checking.
scopes.read: Read check results and search published fact-checks.

auth.serverOnly: Never put an API key in a web page, mobile app or public repository. Call the API from your own server and revoke any key that may have leaked.

rate.title: Rate limits
rate.body: Each key can make {limit} requests per hour. Every response reports your remaining allowance. When you go over it, the API answers 429 Too Many Requests: wait for the number of seconds in Retry-After before trying again.

headers.limit: Requests allowed per hour for this key.
headers.remaining: Requests left in the current hour.
headers.reset: When the allowance resets, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.
headers.retryAfter: Sent with 429 responses: seconds to wait before retrying.

submit.title: Submit a check
submit.body: Send one item for verification. Use JSON for text, links and articles, and multipart/form-data for media files. The response arrives immediately with a tracking ID; the check itself takes about 10 seconds for text and up to a minute for media.

fields.content: The text to check. Up to {textMax} characters for text, {articleMax} for an article. Required for text and article.
fields.url: A full http or https link to a news article or web page. Required for url.
fields.file: The photo, voice note or video, up to {size}. JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG, AAC, MP4, MOV, WebM or 3GP. Required for media.
fields.headline: Optional article headline, up to {max} characters.
fields.language: Language of the content: en, lg, ach, nyn, teo, or auto to detect it (the default).

status.title: Get a result
status.body: Returns the state of a check. When the status is completed, the result field holds the full fact-check object. Tracking IDs look like ZL-7K3P-Q9.

states.queued: Received and waiting to be analysed.
states.processing: Claims are being cross-checked against trusted sources and AI-detection models.
states.failed: The check could not be completed. The error field explains why.

search.title: Search fact-checks
search.body: Search the public library of completed fact-checks. Results are ranked by Community Confidence Score and recency, and verdicts suspended for review are left out.

params.q: Words to look for in titles, summaries and checked text.
params.category: Filter by topic, such as Health or Elections.
params.language: Filter by the language of the checked content.
params.dates: Only checks made on or after, and on or before, these dates (YYYY-MM-DD).
params.perPage: Results per page, from 1 to 50. Default 20.

factCheck.title: Fact-check object
factCheck.body: Completed checks and search results share this shape. Arrays may be empty; fields may be added before v1 but not removed.

fields.id: Permanent ID of the published fact-check.
fields.trackingId: The tracking ID returned when the content was submitted.
fields.confidence: How confident Zuula is in the verdict, from 0 to 100.
fields.summary: A plain-language explanation of the verdict.
fields.findings: Short statements of what is false and what is actually true.
fields.claims: Claims found in the text, with character offsets, an assessment, the reason and the citations that back it.
fields.citations: Sources used, with name, title, link, publication date and stance: supports, contradicts or context.
fields.aiSignals: Checks for AI-generated or manipulated content, each with a score, the threshold and the method.
fields.community: Accurate and inaccurate rating counts from the public, journalists and experts.
fields.humanReview: Present when an expert confirmed or overrode the verdict, with their justification.

errors.title: Errors
errors.body: Errors use standard HTTP status codes and a JSON body with a machine-readable code and a human-readable message.

codes.bad_request: The request is malformed or a required field is missing.
codes.unauthorized: The API key is missing, invalid or revoked.
codes.forbidden: The key does not have the scope this endpoint needs.
codes.not_found: No check or fact-check has that ID.
codes.file_too_large: The media file is larger than 50 MB.
codes.unsupported_media: The file type is not accepted.
codes.invalid_content: The content is too short, too long or not a valid link.
codes.rate_limited: The key has used its hourly allowance. Wait for Retry-After seconds.
codes.server_error: Something went wrong on our side. Try again later.

report.title: Get a fact-check
report.body: Returns one published fact-check by its ID: the same data behind the public <link>report page</link>, including the verdict, confidence, explanation, citations and community ratings.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.body: Planned alongside the API so you don't have to poll: a callback to your server when a check's verdict is ready. This section will be filled in once webhook delivery is designed in Phase 2. The Zuula bots on <link>WhatsApp and Telegram</link> are being built on the same infrastructure.

access.title: Get access
access.body: Verified journalists and administrators can create a key today in <keys>Account → API access</keys>; it works against sample data until the backend ships. For a newsroom integration or a higher rate limit, email <email>hello@zuula.ug</email>. Using the API means accepting the <terms>API terms</terms>.
